diffs.diff: header pin 2 (COM): part says gnd, datasheet reading says io
diffs.evidence: Same physical lug, different 'role' label for a passive contact. The MTS series datasheet lists 'MTS-102  ON - ON  SPDT  3P', 'Rating : 6A 125VAC ; 3A 250VAC': a mechanical SPDT switch with no supply and no chip, so none of its three lugs has an electrical role of its own; the middle lug is the common (moving) contact that the SPDT 3P drawing joins to one outer lug in each lever position. Both readings agree on pin order L1, COM, L2 and that pin 2 is COM. The second reading tags every lug generically as 'io'; the part tags COM 'gnd' because its recommended wiring ties the common contact to ground and reads L1/L2 on GPIOs with the internal pull-up (closed = 0). That is a valid, safe wiring (the switch only ever connects a pulled-up pin to GND, never drives a pin), consistent with the already-published limit switch, whose COM terminal is also role 'gnd'. No pinout or electrical change.
